problem: Measure learning and forgetting when a manipulation policy encounters sequential tasks with incomplete access to past demonstrations.
contribution: LIBERO defines a procedural task-generation framework and controlled task suites for spatial, object, goal and longer-horizon transfer, with lifelong-learning algorithms and multiple policy architectures.
algorithm: Generate language, scene layouts and PDDL goals from behavior templates. Train behavior-cloned policies sequentially, comparing experience replay, EWC and PackNet to sequential finetuning and multitask references. Evaluate success-based forward transfer, negative backward transfer and area-under-curve metrics.
observations: Workspace/wrist images, robot proprioception and task-language embeddings; temporal backbones aggregate partially observed history.
actions: Continuous end-effector actions sampled from a GMM head; not direct cross-embodiment joint copying.
embodiment_and_data: Simulation benchmark; 130 standardized tasks: three 10-task controlled suites plus LIBERO-100 split into90 short and10 long tasks. Provides50 human-teleoperated demonstrations per task.
experiments: Compares ResNet-RNN, ResNet-Transformer and ViT-Transformer across task suites and lifelong algorithms. Investigates task ordering, language embeddings and offline pretraining; source outcomes are simulated task successes, not physical transfer.
baselines: Sequential finetuning, multitask learning, experience replay, EWC and PackNet. Multitask access is a reference with different historical-data access, not an equal-memory sequential method.

quantitative_result.value: LIBERO-GOAL ResNet-T: PackNet NBT0.06±0.01 versus ER0.34±0.02; AUC0.75±0.01 versus0.49±0.02. Means and standard errors over3seeds.
quantitative_result.location: PDF p7 Table1; metric definitions p6 Eq3
quantitative_result.meaning: NBT/AUC aggregate success-derived metrics, not single-trial success probabilities or physical rates.

limitations: A simulator benchmark with a fixed action space and common embodiment does not establish physical or cross-embodiment lifelong learning. Checkpoint selection uses the best evaluated current-task epoch, affecting metric interpretation. Neural architecture and task ordering materially affect conclusions; pretraining can harm downstream learning.
code_and_license: Official Lifelong-Robot-Learning/LIBERO metadata verified: MIT, master commit8f1084e3132a39270c3a13ebe37270a43ece2a01. Repository metadata inspected; no core benchmark source execution is claimed by this review.
hardware_adaptation: Reuse evaluation structure, task-by-task retention matrices and controlled shifts. Record camera/robot/action schemas and physical-session splits independently. Small Explorer tests are not LIBERO scores unless the actual benchmark/task versions are run.
algorithm_detail: The paper FWT averages eleven success measurements across epochs0..50; NBT averages performance loss across subsequent learning stages; AUC combines learning-curve transfer with later retention. These differ from final-stage signed BWT and max-past forgetting. Best-current-task checkpoint selection is part of the published metric protocol.
integration_contract: Store checkpoint-by-task-by-epoch attempted/success/unknown counts and task order. Name exact formulas in each protocol. Explorer's retention_metrics reports final BWT/forgetting and must not relabel these as LIBERO NBT/FWT without implementing the published formulas.
license_evidence: GitHub primary repository metadata returned MIT and exact pinned master revision; see UPSTREAM_AUDIT.json. Dataset assets and downstream dependencies require their own license checks.
required_experiments: At least sequential-finetune versus fixed-budget replay across multiple task orders with matched demonstration counts; frozen evaluations of every prior task after each task; disclose memory/compute/checkpoint selection and uncertainty, plus untouched final sessions.
difference_from_explorer: Task retention and controlled evaluation are established prior art. Explorer's domain-separated ledger and deployment constraints are engineering design until supported by measured ablations.

evidence_locations.supports: Exact metric definitions and checkpoint selection
